Shri Atul Gupta - Advocate for appellant.

Shri Rajendra Singh Yadav - Public Prosecutor for respo
Shri Girdhar Gopal Shivhare - Advocate for complainant.

Appellant has filed this criminal appeal
under Section 14-A (2) of the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act,
1989 against the order dated 30.05.2024 passed by Special Judge(Atrocities), Gwalior, whereby bail
application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. filed on behalf of appellant has been dismissed by the trial
Court.
Appellant has been arrested on 29.05.2024 by Police Station Thatipur District Gwalior in
connection with Crime No.244/2024 registered in relation to the offences punishable under
Sections 376 (2) (n), 354 (x), 294, 506 of Ipc and Section 3 (2) (v) & 3(1)(w)(ii) and Section 3 (2) (v)
of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: As per prosecution case, the allegation of rape is alleged against present appellant.

The prosecutrix,
aged about 30 years, is a lady deserted by husband along with her children and the appellant, on the false promise of marriage won her confidence and committed sexual intercourse with her on various ocassions.
It is the submission of learned counsel for the appellant that false case has been registered against the appellant and he is facing confinement since 29.05.2024.
The chance of tampering with evidence / witness is remote.
Story indicates that it is a case of consent.
Confinement amounts to pretrial detention.
He undertakes to cooperate in trial and not to be a source of harassment or 2 CRA-6728-2024 embarrassment to the complainant party in any manner and that he will not move in her vicinity.
On these grounds prayer for bail is made out.

Learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer and prayed for rejection of appeal by submitting that the appellant prepared objectionable video of the prosecutrix and committed rape upon her and investigation is pending.
Heard.

Considering the submissions and fact situation and looking to the period of custody, without commenting on the merits of case while setting aside order dated 30.05.2024 passed by trial Court,
appeal is allowed and it is directed that appellant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 50,000/-
(Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of like amount to the satisfaction of Trial Court.
The appellant will not leave India without previous permission of the trial Court/Investigating Officer, as the case may be.
Appeal stands allowed and disposed of.
Copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for information compliance.
Certified copy as per rules.
